title: Prediction-Market Newsletter & SEO Growth Plan
purpose: Machine-readable handoff spec for an AI agent to implement a Polymarket-data-driven newsletter/blog plus a programmatic SEO content layer inside an existing prediction-market web app (separate repo).

instructions: This spec is stack-agnostic where possible. The reference implementation context was Next.js (App Router) + React + Tailwind + Supabase, but adapt to the target repo's actual framework.
Before implementing, detect the target repo's framework, rendering model, data store, and existing SEO setup, then map each requirement onto the available primitives.
The single most important technical requirement: data that earns rankings MUST be present in server-rendered HTML (SSR/SSG/ISR). Do not rely on client-side rendering for indexable content.
Never hardcode secrets or private keys. Use environment variables for all API keys and credentials.
Respect Polymarket API rate limits. Cache all data in a datastore; never block page render on a live third-party API call.
openInputsNeeded: Target repo framework & rendering capabilities (Next.js, Remix, SvelteKit, Astro, Rails, etc.)
Existing datastore (Supabase/Postgres/other) and whether Polymarket data is already ingested
Email service provider choice (Resend, Buttondown, Beehiiv, etc.)
Primary domain and whether Google Search Console is set up
Brand voice constraints / existing design system

context.product: A prediction-market web application centered on Polymarket smart-money / copy-trading data.
dataAssets: Smart-money consensus signals (which top traders agree on which market outcomes)
Trader success scores and per-category accuracy (e.g. Wilson score by sport/topic)
Whale positions (largest single positions opened by tracked traders)
Market price history (CLOB midpoint over time)

notes: Gamma /markets and /events hard-cap limit at 100; paginate with offset.
CLOB /markets/{conditionId} tokens carry a 'winner' boolean used for resolution/accuracy scoring.
Use the leaderboard endpoint as a health check (no /health endpoint exists).
On HTTP 429, back off and increase polling interval.

apiResearch.summary: Live probe (2026-06-06) of the Polymarket APIs to catalog the full field surface and undocumented endpoints. The recipes below depend on these. Several of these endpoints/fields are NOT in the reference repo's existing client and unlock the highest-value insights.

verifiedEndpoints.value: PLATFORM-WIDE LIVE WHALE TAPE. Without a user filter + with filterAmount, returns every large aggressive trade across all of Polymarket. Taker side = paid for urgency = conviction signal.
Top holders per outcome with names + share amounts. Enables concentration/fragility analysis and 'who actually holds this' composition.

Full position lifecycle. REDEEM = trader CLAIMED winnings (realized cash, proven win). REWARD = liquidity-mining (not directional skill). Lets you separate realized skill from paper/mark-to-market gains, and detect LPs vs directional bettors.
Live portfolio value for a wallet.
Full order-book depth. Enables slippage-to-deploy-$X, support/resistance walls, and bid/ask depth imbalance (order-flow pressure).
Bid/ask spread = market efficiency + tradeability proxy.
Momentum (price changes), mispricing (lastTradePrice vs bestBid/Ask), liquidity (spread/openInterest), hype (commentCount), and recurring-series detection - mostly without even hitting the CLOB.
verifiedEndpoints.notInReferenceClient: partial - reference client uses /markets but not these fields

verifiedEndpoints.value: Time series for volatility, momentum, and mean-reversion analysis.

activityTypes.REDEEM: Claimed winnings on a resolved market = realized win.

strategicThesis.summary: Turn proprietary Polymarket trader-behavior data into original, recurring, structured content. This is content that does not currently exist online and is therefore both rankable and citable.

threeLayers.rationale: Markets resolve constantly, creating an infinite self-replenishing content supply. Weekly cadence signals an active, authoritative site; each resolved market is a new publishable fact.
Every market, trader, and category is a potential indexable URL. One data pipeline yields thousands of long-tail pages (classic programmatic SEO, like real-estate listing sites).

Prediction markets are finance-adjacent YMYL content where trust signals are decisive. Publicly grading past calls (a settled scorecard) is the strongest trust-builder: experience, expertise, and accountability combined.

guidingPrinciples: Original data beats commentary. The moat is the numbers nobody else surfaces; prose is the human wrapper that makes it linkable.
Build 'linkable assets' (citable reference pages) not just posts. Ask of every piece: would a journalist or another site cite this?
Map content to search intent tiers: informational (evergreen explainers), navigational/entity (programmatic pages), transactional/decision (closest to product).
Rendering is the silent killer: indexable data must be in server-rendered HTML.
Newsletter + SEO are one flywheel: every post is a permanent indexable URL AND an email; site -> signup -> email -> shares/links back.
Optimize for AI answers (GEO): declarative factual sentences, structured data, explicit dates, so LLMs and AI Overviews cite you verbatim.

insightRecipes.summary: Creative route combinations that produce conclusions a reader cannot get from Polymarket's own UI (because each requires JOINING routes). The throughline: 'what does the smart money know that the price doesn't reflect yet - and can I act on it?'. Each recipe is a reusable content+data unit: it powers a newsletter segment AND a programmatic page AND a structured-data block. Recipes 1, 2, 5, and 8 are the strongest core; recipe 5 (calibration) is the flagship link-earning asset.
implementationNotes: Cache all inputs in the datastore; never call these APIs in a page's render hot path.
Every numeric claim in generated prose must trace to a stored value (no LLM-invented figures).
Store each recipe's output with a timestamp so the Settled Scorecard can grade it later.
Most recipes map 1:1 to a JSON-LD block (Article/Dataset/FAQPage) for AI-answer citation.

recipes.title: The Mispricing Gap (smart money vs. the price)
recipes.question: Where are top traders positioned away from where the market is priced?
recipes.method: Compute a size-weighted 'smart-money implied price' from top-trader entries on a market, then subtract current market price. Rank markets by the absolute gap.
recipes.readerTakeaway: Market says 18%, but 7 of the top-20 traders are loading YES at avg 24c - a 6-point smart-money premium.

recipes.title: The Conviction Tape (whale taker feed + book impact)
recipes.question: Who is aggressively betting big right now, and did they move the market?
recipes.method: Stream large taker fills platform-wide. Taker = crossed the spread = paid for urgency. Cross-reference book depth to estimate price impact of the sweep.
recipes.readerTakeaway: A $250k taker buy just swept YES from 0.55 -> 0.61. Someone wanted in now, not at a better price.

recipes.title: Concentration Fragility (who actually holds this)
recipes.question: Is this price held up by broad conviction or a couple of whales who could bail?
recipes.method: Compute share of an outcome held by top-N wallets (Herfindahl-style concentration). High concentration + thin volume = fragile.
recipes.readerTakeaway: 92% of YES is held by 3 wallets. That isn't conviction, it's a cliff.

recipes.title: Paper vs. Proven (realized-skill filter)
recipes.question: Is this leaderboard trader's PnL banked cash or unrealized luck?
recipes.method: Compare realized cash (sum of REDEEM usdcSize) and current /value against leaderboard PnL. Flag traders whose rank is driven by a single open mark-to-market position.
recipes.readerTakeaway: He's #4 on the leaderboard, but 80% of that is one unrealized position. Here's who actually banked it.

recipes.title: The Calibration Truth (platform-wide flagship)
recipes.question: Are Polymarket prices well-calibrated, or are some price bands systematically mispriced?
routes: resolved markets via clob /markets/{conditionId} winner flag
recipes.method: Across a large sample of resolved markets, bucket by price (e.g. 5-10c bands) and compute realized YES frequency per bucket. Plot predicted vs actual = calibration curve.
recipes.readerTakeaway: Heavy favorites (85-95c) resolve YES 96% of the time - the market underprices near-locks.

recipes.title: Move Attribution + Reversion (momentum)
recipes.question: That big price move - was it real flow or one wallet, and will it hold?
recipes.method: For markets with large recent moves, attribute the move to broad flow vs a single dominant trade. Backtest reversion rate of single-wallet-driven moves.
recipes.readerTakeaway: 40 -> 62c in 6 hours, but it was one trader. These round-trip ~70% of the time.

recipes.title: Specialist Edge (don't follow stars blindly)
recipes.question: What is this top trader actually good at - and where should you fade them?
recipes.method: Bucket a trader's resolved trades by inferred category; compute per-category win rate + Wilson score. Contrast with their overall rank.
recipes.readerTakeaway: Follow Theo4 on politics (71%), fade him on sports (48%).

recipes.title: Is the Edge Tradeable? (the honesty layer)
recipes.question: Can a normal person actually enter this signal without moving the price?
recipes.method: Given a target $ size, walk the order book to compute realized slippage and effective entry price. Combine with spread to label edges 'tradeable' or 'illiquid'.
recipes.readerTakeaway: Signal's real, but YES has $400 of depth - you'd move it 4c buying in. Skip.

recipes.title: Near-Lock Yield (theta framing)
recipes.question: Which soon-to-resolve markets offer low-risk short-duration return?
recipes.method: Filter markets resolving within N days priced > X cents; compute implied return = (1 - price)/price, annualized by days-to-resolution. Cross-check liquidity.
recipes.readerTakeaway: 11 markets resolving this week priced >95c - here's the implied annualized 'yield' if they hold.

recipes.title: Neg-Risk Arbitrage (where it exists)
recipes.question: Do the outcomes of a multi-candidate event sum to more than 100%?
recipes.method: For negRisk events, sum the YES prices of all mutually-exclusive outcomes. Sum > 1 implies an overround that can be faded; flag the spread.
recipes.readerTakeaway: These 4 candidates sum to 1.08 - an 8% overround you can fade.

recipes.title: Hype Trap (social vs. smart money)
recipes.question: Is this trending market backed by sharps or just retail noise?
recipes.method: Flag markets with high commentCount and retail volume spikes but zero top-ranked traders in /holders.
recipes.readerTakeaway: Most-commented market of the week - and not a single top-50 trader is in it.

workstreams.goal: Make content server-rendered, well-described, and discoverable. Nothing ranks without this.

requirements.requirement: Render headline content (top signals, top traders, weekly summary) in server-rendered HTML. Push interactive widgets into isolated client components.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: View-source (JS disabled) shows the primary content text and key data values, not an empty shell.

requirements.requirement: Per-route metadata: unique title (with template), description, canonical URL, Open Graph + Twitter card tags.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Every indexable route returns unique <title>, meta description, canonical, and og/twitter tags.

requirements.requirement: Auto-generate branded social share images per post/market/trader (e.g. '6 sharps are on YES @ 62c').
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Each post/market/trader URL exposes a unique og:image rendered from live data.

requirements.requirement: Generate sitemap.xml (all posts, markets, traders, categories) and robots.txt.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Sitemap submitted to Google Search Console; robots allows crawl of public content and points to sitemap.

requirements.requirement: JSON-LD: Article (posts), FAQPage (market explainers), BreadcrumbList (navigation), Dataset (leaderboard).
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Pages validate in Google Rich Results Test with no errors.

workstreams.goal: Stand up the blog routes and publish one hand-tuned issue to lock the editorial voice.

requirements.requirement: Indexable blog index + /blog/[slug] post routes, server-rendered.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Posts are crawlable, have full metadata, and interlink to related markets/traders.

requirements.requirement: Posts stored as MDX files or a 'blog_posts' table (title, slug, body, published_at, segments, cited entity IDs).
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: A post can be created, rendered, and linked from sitemap.

requirements.requirement: Produce one fully hand-tuned issue from real data as the canonical voice/style reference.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Human-approved sample issue exists for the generator to emulate.

workstreams.goal: Automatically build weekly issues from stored data on a schedule.

requirements.requirement: Query datastore for the week's standout data per segment (top consensus, reversals, whale moves, settled results).
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: A single job assembles all segment inputs without live API calls in the hot path.

requirements.requirement: Deterministic templates per segment + optional LLM polish for narrative voice (guardrailed to the data).
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Generated draft is factually grounded in queried data; numbers are never fabricated.

requirements.requirement: Run on a schedule (cron / scheduled function / CI workflow). Fresh content shipped weekly.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: A new post is created and published automatically each cycle.

requirements.requirement: Send the same content to the email list via the chosen ESP.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Published post triggers an email send to subscribers.

workstreams.goal: Scale to thousands of unique, indexable, interlinked pages from the data pipeline.

pageTemplates.purpose: Per-market page: question, live odds, smart-money positioning, price-history chart, plain-language explainer.
pageTemplates.uniquenessRule: Must include genuinely distinct per-market data (odds history, positioning) to avoid thin/doorway content.

pageTemplates.purpose: Public trader profile: success score, category proficiency, recent calls, win rate.
Category hub aggregating markets + signals (NBA, politics, crypto, etc.).

requirements.requirement: Use static generation + incremental revalidation (or equivalent) so pages are server-rendered and refreshed on a sane interval.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Pages serve cached HTML, revalidate on schedule, and reflect updated data.

requirements.requirement: Dense interlinking: post -> markets -> traders -> categories -> back to posts.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Every template links to its related entities; orphan pages are minimized.

requirements.requirement: Suppress or noindex pages lacking sufficient unique data.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Pages below a data-richness threshold are not indexed.

requirements.requirement: Handle resolved-market decay: consolidate/redirect old markets into a historical track record rather than letting them rot.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Resolved markets remain useful (track record) or redirect; no large set of dead thin pages.

workstreams.goal: Build compounding growth loops and measurement.

requirements.requirement: Newsletter signup form on-site (homepage + post footers).
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Visitors can subscribe; subscribers stored in ESP.

requirements.requirement: Shareable cards + 'embed this' widgets for the consensus board to earn backlinks.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Each signal/market has share link + OG image; an embeddable widget exists.

requirements.requirement: Wire up Google Search Console + lightweight analytics from day one.
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Indexed pages, impressions, and scorecard accuracy are tracked.

pitfalls.risk: Thin programmatic pages flagged as doorway content
pitfalls.mitigation: Each page must carry genuinely distinct data; noindex insufficient ones.
Cache aggressively in datastore; never block render on live API.
Force SSR/SSG/ISR for anything that must rank.
Templates grounded in queried data; LLM only polishes prose, never invents figures.

constraints: No secrets or private keys in code; environment variables only.
Respect Polymarket API rate limits and 429 backoff.
Generated content must be factually grounded in stored data.
Adapt all framework-specific guidance to the target repo's actual stack.
